chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Rayyān, who said:
I wrote to al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom. It has been narrated to us that there is nothing of the world for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله except al-khums.”
So the reply came: “Indeed, the world and whatever is upon it belongs to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly realm or the world
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرِيِّ: al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام, the Imam to whom the written question was addressed
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله have a right only to khums, or to the whole world and what is in it?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written question to al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام regarding the claim that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله possessed from the world only khums. The response states that the world and all that is upon it belongs to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, indicating his comprehensive divine authority and right.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Al Rayyan who said,
‘I wrote to Al-Askaryasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! It is reported to us that there isn’t anything for Rasool-Allahazwj from the world except for the fifth (Khums)’.
So the answer came: ‘The world and whatever is upon it is for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan who has said the following.

“I wrote to abu Muhammad, al-Hassan, al-‘Askari (a.s.), May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, it is narrated to us that nothing else from this world belongs to the Messenger of Allah except one fifth of net income.”
The answer that came said, “Certainly, the world and all that is in it belong to the Messenger of Allah.”
